name: Handle screen-outs and non-productive time on a frac pad
summary: When pumping stops on a frac pad, because a stage screens out, a pump fails, sand, water or wireline are not ready, or weather closes in, the treater and field supervisor have to decide quickly how to recover: flush, flow the well back, call in coiled tubing, swap a pump or wait. While they do, the whole fleet and a crew of about twenty stand by. Afterwards the lost time is recorded and the supervisor and the customer's wellsite supervisor agree who pays for it under the master service agreement; disagreements go to the operations manager and the producer's completions superintendent and can hold up the field ticket for weeks.

baseline.org_archetype: A TSX-listed Canadian pressure pumping company with six to eight 24-hour frac crews working for producers in Alberta and northeast BC, run from district bases with a Calgary head office.
baseline.notes: Modelled on the organisation file oilfield-services-co (composite based on Trican and STEP Canada). 2020 was a deep downturn and sits at the low end of volume ranges.

unit_of_work: one non-productive time event (a stoppage of pumping on a pad)
trigger: Pumping stops unplanned during a frac job: a screen-out, an equipment failure, a third-party or supply delay, or weather. The job execution process flags it with a non-productive time report.
end_state: Pumping has resumed, the stop and start times and cause are recorded, responsibility is agreed with the customer and reflected on the field ticket, the report is sent to the customer and technical services, any failed unit has a repair request, and the event has been through the operations manager's weekly NPT review.

volume.seasonality: Follows frac activity; weather events cluster in January cold snaps and summer thunderstorms.

surge.cause: Winter completion peak while frozen ground allows access to muskeg leases (January to mid-March)

evidence.note: Same surge as the organisation file's process map entry (crews fully booked January to mid-March); the multiplier is an estimate from quarterly proppant swings of 260,000-479,000 tonnes in the organisation file.

Organisation file process map volume (about 0.5 events per well at 50 wells a month). The job execution workflow branches give about 0.4 stoppages per well; the difference is short stoppages that are logged but not modelled there.

Email, Microsoft Teams and mobile phones
Electronic field ticketing on tablets, linked to the ERP price book
Maintenance work order and equipment history module

resources.name: Crewed hydraulic fracturing fleet (pumps, blender, data van, sand and chemical units, treating iron)
Frac pump unit (2,500 to 3,000 HHP, trailer mounted)

steps.name: Stop pumping and secure the well
steps.description: The treater sees the stoppage on the data van, calls the pumps down or confirms they have tripped, closes the wellhead valve if pressure is near the limit and tells the field supervisor and the wellsite supervisor what happened.

control.basis: Maximum allowable treating pressure and wellhead rating from the treatment design

evidence.note: Typical first response; time estimated.

steps.name: Bring pumps offline and bleed the lines
steps.description: Pump operators take their pumps out of gear, close the plug valves to isolate them and bleed pressure off the treating iron to the flowback tank under the treater's direction, keeping everyone out of the red zone.

error.defect_description: A line is opened before it is fully bled.

control.basis: Company energy isolation and bleed-off procedure for high-pressure treating iron (Alberta OHS Code hazardous energy control)

evidence.note: Operators run high-pressure pumping equipment from control panels (alis profile); crew size estimated.

steps.name: Classify the cause of the stoppage
steps.description: The field supervisor and treater look at the pressure chart, the pump alarms and what the crew saw, and decide which kind of stoppage it is: a screen-out, an equipment failure, a third-party or supply delay, or weather. The cause decides who will be asked to pay for the lost time.

error.defect_description: The cause is recorded wrongly, for example a pump failure logged as a screen-out.

evidence.note: Cause shares are estimates; causes as listed in the organisation file process description.

steps.name: Choose the screen-out recovery plan
steps.description: The treater looks at how much proppant is in the wellbore and the pressure behaviour and proposes a recovery: overflush with clean fluid, flow the well back to the tank to clear the perforations, or a coiled tubing cleanout if the plug and casing are covered with sand.

error.defect_description: Flowback is tried when a cleanout was needed, adding hours.

evidence.note: Common recovery options; the organisation file names flushing and calling coiled tubing.

steps.name: Customer approves the recovery plan
steps.description: The customer's wellsite supervisor discusses the plan with their completions engineer in town and approves the flowback or orders a coiled tubing unit. The decision is the producer's because the well and the extra cost are theirs.

evidence.note: Producer approval of well interventions is standard; time estimated.

steps.name: Flow the well back to clear the perforations
steps.description: The flowback crew opens the well to the flowback tank through the choke so sand in the wellbore is carried out, while the treater watches pressure to see whether the perforations are open again.

evidence.note: Flowback success share and duration are estimates.

steps.name: Wait for a coiled tubing cleanout
steps.description: A coiled tubing unit is called out, rigged up on the well and runs in to wash the sand out down to the plug, then rigs off so the frac crew can resume. The frac fleet stands by unless it can keep pumping another well on the pad.

evidence.note: Coiled tubing is used as contingency for screen-outs (organisation file); mobilisation and run times estimated.

steps.name: Diagnose the failed unit
steps.description: Pump operators open the failed pump or blender component and find the fault: a washed fluid end, a failed valve or seat, an engine or transmission fault, a cracked iron connection. They decide with the supervisor whether it can be fixed on location.

control.basis: Company energy isolation and bleed-off procedure for high-pressure treating iron (Alberta OHS Code hazardous energy control)

next.condition: fixed or swapped by the crew
a mechanic or parts are needed

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Call out a field mechanic and parts
steps.description: The field supervisor phones the maintenance shop for a field mechanic and parts, describes the fault and opens a repair request; the mechanic drives out from the district base.

evidence.note: Field breakdown support is a separate process in the organisation file; times estimated.

steps.name: Swap in the standby pump or repair on location
steps.description: Operators isolate and disconnect the failed unit, connect the standby pump to the manifold or replace the failed part, then pressure test the connections before the unit goes back on line.

error.defect_description: A connection leaks on restart and is redone.

control.basis: Company energy isolation and bleed-off procedure for high-pressure treating iron (Alberta OHS Code hazardous energy control)

evidence.note: Estimate; the wait covers a mechanic's drive when one was called.

steps.name: Chase the third party and log standby
steps.description: The supervisor calls whoever is holding up the job (the wireline crew, the water transfer contractor, the sand coordinator or the fuel supplier), gets a time estimate, tells the customer and logs the standby start time.

evidence.note: STEP reported extended delays on a client location from challenging well conditions in Q4 2021; durations estimated.

steps.name: Hold for weather and protect the equipment
steps.description: In extreme cold the crew keeps fluid moving or drains lines so nothing freezes; for lightning or high wind everyone moves away from the iron. The supervisor decides when to restart with the wellsite supervisor.

control.basis: Company lightning and cold weather stop-work rules

evidence.note: Weather delays in Canadian frac operations in December 2021 and January 2022 (STEP).

steps.name: Restart pumping and confirm a stable treatment
steps.description: The treater brings the pumps back to rate, watches pressure until the treatment is stable and decides with the wellsite supervisor whether to finish the interrupted stage as designed or with a reduced proppant ramp.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Record stop and start times, cause and units affected
steps.description: The data technician marks the stop and restart times in the acquisition record and copies them, with the cause and units affected, into the non-productive time log spreadsheet for the pad.

error.defect_description: Times are rounded or copied wrongly.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Write the NPT report with pressure charts
steps.description: The treater writes a short report: what happened, the sequence of events, pressure and rate charts from the data van, actions taken and the hours lost, in the company template.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Review the report and propose who pays
steps.description: The field supervisor checks the report against the log and proposes how the hours are charged under the master service agreement: standby billed to the customer for third-party or well-caused delays, no charge for the company's equipment failures, and shared or negotiated time for screen-outs.

control.basis: Master service agreement standby and non-productive time terms

evidence.note: The organisation file notes that NPT disputes hit field tickets; allocation rules are common MSA practice.

steps.name: Agree responsibility with the wellsite supervisor
steps.description: At the morning meeting or the next quiet moment the supervisor goes through the report with the customer's wellsite supervisor and asks them to accept the proposed charges.

evidence.note: Dispute share estimated.

steps.name: Operations manager reviews the disputed event
steps.description: The frac operations manager reads the report and data, checks the MSA terms and the customer's history of similar events, and decides what the company will accept.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Negotiate with the producer's completions superintendent
steps.description: The operations manager calls or meets the producer's completions superintendent, walks through the evidence and agrees a split of the hours, often trading some standby for goodwill on the program.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Update the field ticket with standby or no-charge lines
steps.description: The field supervisor adds the agreed standby hours or marks the lost hours as no charge on the tablet field ticket and notes the agreement reference.

error.defect_description: Standby hours are keyed differently from what was agreed.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Send the NPT report to the customer and technical services
steps.description: The treater emails the final report to the producer and saves it in the job folder, where technical services pick it up for job analysis and repeat-failure tracking.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Open a repair work order for the failed unit
steps.description: The supervisor enters a repair request in the maintenance system for the failed pump or component with the fault description and hours, so the shop can rebuild it at the next move.

error.defect_description: The fault description is too vague for the shop.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Review the NPT log for repeat causes
steps.description: Each week the operations manager reads the NPT log across crews, looks for repeat failures by unit, customer or cause, and raises maintenance or planning changes. Time shown is this event's share.

next.condition: hours charged to the customer in whole or part

evidence.note: Weekly review cadence and charge split are estimates.

exceptions.name: Screen-out needing coiled tubing
exceptions.description: Flowback fails and a coiled tubing unit cleans out the well.

exceptions.name: Mechanic callout
exceptions.description: An equipment failure needs a field mechanic and parts.

exceptions.name: Disputed NPT
exceptions.description: The customer disputes the charge and managers negotiate.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from stoppage to agreed NPT, report sent and weekly review done

evidence.note: Estimate: most events are resolved on location within hours and agreed at the next morning meeting (about 1-2 days), then wait on average two to three days for the weekly review; disputes that wait for managers stretch the tail to two weeks or more.

benchmarks.unit: hours of pumping per 24-hour day, the rest being between-stage time and NPT

pain_points.description: The whole fleet and crew stand by during every stoppage, at about $3,000 an hour of fleet cost plus crew wages.

evidence.note: Fleet cost per hour from the organisation file; standby durations estimated.

pain_points.description: A screen-out that needs coiled tubing costs most of a day or more while a unit is found and rigged up.

evidence.note: Estimate.

pain_points.description: Who pays for lost time is argued after the fact from loosely kept logs, and disputes hold up the field ticket and the invoice.

evidence.note: The organisation file process description notes that NPT disputes hit field tickets.

sources.title: STEP Energy Services Ltd. Reports Fourth Quarter and Year End 2021 Results
sources.supports: Canadian fracturing 2021: 977 operating days and 1,012,000 tonnes of proppant (about 1,040 tonnes per operating day); 704 days and 776,000 tonnes in 2020; four spreads with 200,000 HP; Q4 2021 work hit by extended delays on a client location from challenging well conditions and by late-December weather; smaller jobs reduce proppant per day; spring break-up restricts equipment moves.

sources.title: Case Study: Increasing Pumping Hours Through Optimized Operations - STEP Energy Services
sources.supports: Canadian frac pads: average pumping hours per day rose from 14.03 (Q4 2018, three pads) to 18.93 on a four-well pad for one client, and from 15.47 (February 2019) to 17.95 (August 2019) for another; gains from managing maintenance schedules, bi-weekly meetings with operators and pre- and post-pad reviews; post-job data delivered to clients through an online tool.

sources.title: Occupations in Alberta: Well Service Equipment Operator
sources.supports: Pumping services use high-pressure pumping equipment and chemicals, fluids or gases; operators monitor control panels and gauges, may mix materials, assemble and connect equipment, work outdoors in all weather, long hours and much travel; tickets include Energy Safety Canada eGSO, WHMIS, H2S, TDG and first aid; pump operators often need a Class 1 licence.

assumptions: The workflow starts when job execution flags a stoppage; standby fleet time is also shown in the job execution workflow from the well's side, so fleet hours here should not be added to it.
Cause shares (screen-out 30%, equipment 35%, third party 25%, weather 10%) and the dispute rate (28%) are estimates; no published Canadian figures were found.
Frac pump operators and data van technicians take part although the organisation file's process map lists only the treater, supervisor and operations manager.
The weekly NPT review is included as the last step, which adds up to five days of calendar wait to the cycle.
Loaded costs come from the organisation file (base wage x 1.35).
